metadata.title: Chart Atlas: Visual Vocabulary for Managers

sourceNotes.role: 88,409 store-month rows from 2,042 stores; the Part II through-line for seasonality, price, volume, and share.
3,111 counties for cross-sectional distributions, relationships, maps, intervals, and coefficient previews.
51 state time series from 2000-01 through 2026-04 for lines, indexes, and heatmaps.
Small invented arrays only where the chart is a business bridge form rather than a natural field in the three cases.

cards.title: Histogram
cards.useWhen: Show the shape of one numeric variable with counts.
cards.managerQuestion: Are most store-months small, or do a few stores dominate volume?
cards.avoid: Do not compare many groups with overlapping histograms.
cards.caseExample: Soup: Progresso store-month volume is long-tailed.
cards.finding: The median store-month sells 659 units, while the 95th percentile sells 5,476.

cards.title: Density Curve
cards.useWhen: Show a smooth distribution shape when exact bins would distract.
cards.managerQuestion: Where is the typical county in the vote distribution?
cards.avoid: Do not imply precision in thin tails.
cards.caseExample: County: Trump vote share clusters heavily above 50 percent across counties.
cards.finding: The county median is 69.5%, higher than the mean of 66.1%.

cards.title: Box Plot
cards.managerQuestion: Which regions have higher or lower typical county vote shares?
cards.avoid: Do not use it when stakeholders need individual values.
cards.caseExample: County: regional boxes reveal different medians and spreads.
cards.finding: South has the highest regional median county share; East has the lowest.

cards.title: Sorted Bar Chart
cards.useWhen: Rank a small set of categories by one metric.
cards.managerQuestion: Which region has the highest average county vote share?
cards.avoid: Do not use unsorted bars when rank is the message.
cards.caseExample: County: regions sorted by average Trump vote.

cards.title: Dot / Lollipop Plot
cards.useWhen: Compare values precisely without heavy bars.
cards.managerQuestion: Which states had the largest home-value increase since 2020?
cards.avoid: Do not use it for continuous time paths.
cards.caseExample: Zillow: state home-value change from January 2020 to the latest month.
cards.finding: Ohio rose 56.2% since January 2020; Texas rose 35.6%.

cards.title: Line Chart
cards.useWhen: Show how a metric evolves over ordered time.
cards.managerQuestion: How did state home values move through the housing cycle?
cards.avoid: Do not use it for unordered categories.
cards.caseExample: Zillow: California, Texas, Florida, and New York home value paths.
cards.finding: The same housing cycle is visible, but dollar levels remain very different across states.

cards.title: Indexed Time Series
cards.useWhen: Compare growth paths with different starting levels.
cards.managerQuestion: Which housing markets grew faster after 2020?
cards.avoid: Do not read index values as dollars.
cards.caseExample: Zillow: each state equals 100 in January 2020.
cards.finding: Indexing shows relative growth: Ohio leads the selected states after 2020.

cards.title: Small Multiples
cards.useWhen: Repeat the same chart across groups with common scales.
cards.managerQuestion: Do housing cycles look similar across states?
cards.avoid: Do not vary scales silently when magnitude matters.
cards.caseExample: Zillow: four state panels reveal timing and amplitude.
cards.finding: The post-2020 surge appears in every panel, but amplitude and level differ sharply.

cards.title: Scatterplot
cards.useWhen: Show the relationship between two numeric variables.
cards.managerQuestion: Do counties with more college graduates vote differently?
cards.avoid: Do not call a slope causal without a design.
cards.caseExample: County: education share and Trump vote share.
cards.finding: College share and county Trump vote have a strong negative correlation (r = -0.54).

cards.title: Bubble Plot
cards.useWhen: Add magnitude to a two-variable relationship.
cards.managerQuestion: Do the largest-vote counties sit in different density/vote space?
cards.avoid: Do not let bubble area overwhelm the x-y comparison.
cards.caseExample: County: vote count sizes each point.
cards.finding: The largest-vote counties cluster in higher-density space, where county Trump share is usually lower.

cards.title: Choropleth / Tile Map
cards.useWhen: Location is part of the decision.
cards.managerQuestion: Where is the regional pattern strongest?
cards.avoid: Do not map data just because a place field exists.
cards.caseExample: County: state tile map summarizes county vote patterns.
cards.finding: The tile map makes broad regional pattern visible while deliberately hiding within-state county variation.

cards.title: Correlation Matrix
cards.useWhen: Scan many pairwise relationships at once.
cards.managerQuestion: Which demographic variables move together before modeling?
cards.avoid: Do not treat correlation as effect size or causality.
cards.caseExample: County: demographics, density, income, and vote share.
cards.finding: College share correlates -0.54 with county Trump share; white share correlates 0.52.

cards.title: Heatmap
cards.useWhen: Show a matrix of values across two ordered dimensions.
cards.managerQuestion: Which states and years show the biggest housing jumps?
cards.avoid: Do not use color when exact values are the decision.
cards.caseExample: Zillow: annual home-value changes by state and year.
cards.finding: The largest selected state-year jump is Arizona in 2021 at 26.2%.

cards.title: Interval Plot
cards.useWhen: Show estimates with uncertainty in the same visual.
cards.managerQuestion: Does the density-vote pattern look stable enough to discuss?
cards.avoid: Do not hide the denominator behind a precise dot.
cards.caseExample: County: mean Trump vote by population-density decile.
cards.finding: The low- to high-density decile gap is about 34.8 percentage points.

cards.title: Coefficient / Forest Plot
cards.managerQuestion: Which predictors remain visually important after adjustment?
cards.avoid: Do not show coefficients before explaining units and controls.
cards.finding: The largest standardized association is White share (+9.03 points).

cards.title: Pareto Chart
cards.useWhen: Show which categories contribute most of a total.
cards.managerQuestion: Which product families explain most revenue?
cards.avoid: Do not use it when categories are mutually ordered by time.
cards.caseExample: Teaching data: revenue concentration across product families.
cards.finding: The top two product families account for two-thirds of the illustrative total.

cards.title: Waterfall Chart
cards.useWhen: Explain how components bridge from start to finish.
cards.managerQuestion: What moved gross price to net revenue?
cards.avoid: Do not use it for unrelated categories.
cards.caseExample: Teaching data: price bridge from list price to net revenue.
cards.finding: Discounts, margin, and trade spend turn a 100 list-price index into 61 net revenue points.

histogram.domain_note: Binned from 0 to roughly the 99th percentile; extreme right-tail store-months are intentionally clipped for legibility.
